analysis.title: Is the case for commodities still intact?
key_insights: Brent crude has fallen to near USD 95/bbl from as high as USD 118/bbl at end October as markets price a greater chance of Middle East de-escalation and recovering supply.
A stronger-than-expected 'Blue Wave' US midterms outcome has encouraged markets to price in more US-Iran de-escalation.
Middle Eastern oil loadings have recovered substantially from earlier disruption, and softer demand expectations have also weighed on prices.
Lower oil prices do not remove supply constraints and structural demand drivers. Higher insurance and freight costs have raised the delivered cost of crude.
Copper remains supported by constrained supply and long-term demand from power grids, data centers and electrification.
Central bank buying, robust Chinese demand and concerns over rising public debt should continue to support gold, despite high real yields and a firmer US dollar.
Broad commodity exposure may diversify portfolios and protect against risks that challenge both equities and bonds. Leadership can rotate quickly across energy, metals, agriculture and gold.
IEA November projections show the global oil market returning to a surplus in 4Q26, followed by a 'more substantial build in 2027'. Gulf oil exports (excluding Oman) are 26% below pre-war levels.
Global visible oil inventories were 7.8 billion barrels at end-September, more than 500 million barrels below February levels.
UBS favors broad, actively managed commodity exposure, with a preference for copper and strategic gold holdings, sized for price volatility.

sector_views.rationale: Diversification amid geopolitical risks and structural demand from power and AI infrastructure. Preference for copper and strategic gold, with broad actively managed exposure.

macro_indicators.reading: near USD 95/bbl, down from as high as USD 118/bbl at end October
macro_indicators.interpretation: Supply premium has eased on de-escalation hopes, but low inventories and fragile shipping flows leave energy markets vulnerable.

macro_indicators.reading: 7.8 billion barrels at end-September, more than 500 million barrels below February levels
macro_indicators.interpretation: Low inventories leave energy markets vulnerable to supply shocks.
Exports have recovered substantially but remain below pre-war levels.
IEA projection of a return to surplus implies downward pressure on crude prices.

trade_ideas.description: Hold diversified, actively managed broad commodity exposure, with a preference for copper and strategic gold holdings, via indices, ETFs, ETCs or structured investments.
trade_ideas.rationale: Diversification amid geopolitical risks, structural demand from power and AI infrastructure, and protection against risks that challenge both equities and bonds.

risk_factors: Rapid leadership rotation across energy, metals, agriculture and gold.
Commodity price volatility and holding costs.
Fragile shipping flows and low oil inventories leave energy markets vulnerable.
Softer demand expectations weighing on oil prices.
High real yields and a firmer US dollar are headwinds for gold.
vol_and_positioning: Commodities carry unique risks around volatility and holding costs; exposure should be sized for price volatility and regularly rebalanced.
geopolitical: Middle East de-escalation: markets pricing a greater chance of US-Iran de-escalation after the 'Blue Wave' US midterms outcome.
Fragile shipping flows and higher insurance and freight costs in the Middle East raise the delivered cost of crude.
Gulf oil exports (excluding Oman) remain 26% below pre-war levels.
